text:
dmitri: quick heads-up — during the 1M-token long-context perf run I see steady RSS growth on the KV cache that doesn't plateau. looks like fragmentation + small-slot stickiness. dumping allocator snapshot now

caroline: ugh. can you paste the allocator/slot stats and a flamegraph snippet?

ben: is this the thing where tiny allocations never merge back because of slot warmness? we saw similar with the microchunk path a while ago.

alice: curious if this is more eviction-policy or allocator-fragmentation. we should separate concerns: measure eviction churn vs free-list fragmentation.

Dmitri paste: ```
# kv_alloc_stats
slots: total=131072 used=98341 free=32731
slab_buckets: [64: 48221 used=46710 free=1511, 128: 22011 used=17000 free=5000, 256: 16000 used=8000 free=8000, 512+: 44840]
fragmentation_index ~= 0.42  # high
small_slot_reuse_rate: 0.12
avg_kv_live_ttl: 46m
most_long_contexts=chat-stream tests generating many partial caches
```

caroline: that small_slot_reuse_rate is the smoking gun. 12% reuse means we keep holes everywhere. any compaction running?

Dmitri: compactor runs on threshold >0.6 fragmentation, currently configured to be conservative: min_interval=15m, max_batch_bytes=64MB. In these runs fragmentation climbs to ~0.45 then holds, no GC because we hit min_interval.

ben: can we do an opportunistic compact on allocation when a bucket's local free < X? i.e., trigger a mini-compact while allocating to that bucket. tradeoff: CPU spike vs avoid long-term growth.

alice: two knobs to try: 1) bump small bucket block_size from 64->96 or 128 to reduce header overhead and increase contiguous reuse; 2) reduce compactor min_interval to 1m but limit work per second to avoid latency spikes.

caroline: also consider warming policy: prefer reusing recently freed contiguous runs (warmth scoring) instead of strictly LIFO free-list. that can reduce fragmentation by consolidating hot runs.

Dmitri: ran a quick experiment: changed block_size=128 + min_interval=60s + compaction_budget=8MB/s. results on the 1M-token job: peak RSS -12%, steady-state fragmentation index down to 0.31, small_slot_reuse_rate -> 0.27, p95 token latency +2ms.

ben: +2ms p95 seems acceptable in many workloads. what about worst-case tail during compaction? any observed spikes?

Dmitri: small CPU spikes when compactor active, but we bounded it; no request timeouts. biggest impact was increased memory churn in short bursts.

alice: I'd like an AB test: run 50% canary with new params on dedicated fleet for 24h. metrics to collect: fragmentation index, small_slot_reuse_rate, peak RSS, p95/p99 token latency, compaction CPU % and error rate.

infra-bot: canary created: cluster=canary-rw-03, rollout=50%, started 2025-06-04T14:03:30Z. monitors: kv-frag-index, kv-rss, request-p95.

caroline: also add a microbenchmark: synthetic workload that interleaves many long contexts with many short ones to measure cross-scenario regression. include a variant that pins eviction to LRU vs our TTL-based policy.

ben: one more idea — split small bucket into two age-segregated pools: hot_small and cold_small. allocate hot for recent donors and only promote to cold after N frees. this reduces interleaving of long-lived and short-lived objects. complexity is moderate.

dmitri: noted. next steps: 1) run canary with block_size=128 + compactor 60s budgeted; 2) run synthetic cross-workload microbench; 3) prototype hot/cold split in a branch and measure. I'll post perf dashboard link after 6h of canary.

alice: SGTM. please also capture allocation traces for any compaction-induced latency spikes.

dmitri: will do, uploading initial graphs: https://redwood-internal/perf/d/kv/1749123456-alloc-frag?orgId=1

caroline: thanks — keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
